subject: AuroraField adapter assimilation & validation

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@aurorafield.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: AuroraField — adapter submission & validation request

Hi Diego,

Thanks for taking a first look at AuroraField's connector for Redwood. We're an ISV that provides domain-specific embeddings and a lightweight retrieval layer; we've built a prototype adapter that targets Redwood's caching and batching primitives and would like to go through your partner validation so we can be listed as a verified partner.

What we're asking for:
- Guidance on the validation checklist you run for partners (compatibility, auth, perf).
- A short tech sync (30–45m) with partner engineering to discuss runtime assumptions.
- A small sandbox slot to run smoke tests against a Redwood dev runtime (non-prod).

Context: our adapter does two non-standard things — streaming token-level reranker hooks and a token-preserving auth handshake that exchanges a short-lived signed assertion. We want to make sure those patterns map cleanly to Redwood runtime fallbacks and don't break caching behavior.

Happy to share the design doc and an auth-flow PNG.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Head of Integrations, AuroraField
attachments: aurorafield-connector-design.pdf; auth-flow.png

Hi Maya — great to meet you (virtually).

Thanks for the overview. We're interested in validating the adapter; there are a few quick questions before the sync:
- Can you confirm the expected p99 latency targets for single-request retrieval+rank (ms)?
- Do you expect any long-lived connections or sticky state per-client?
- Will the signed assertion be validated by Redwood, or by your runtime?

I've looped in Kim from Partner Solutions who will own the sandbox run and the test matrix. Would 30m on Tue (PDT) work for a technical sync?

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Partner Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Integrations Team <integrations@aurorafield.com>

Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AuroraField — adapter submission & validation request

Diego / Kim,

Thanks — attaching the design doc and auth-flow graphic (see attachments). Quick answers inline:
- p99 target for retrieval+rank: 220–300ms for 512-token contexts (happy to tune).
- No long-lived sticky state; per-request ephemeral keys are used.
- The signed assertion is minted by AuroraField and validated by Redwood during the adapter handshake; we can move validation to our side if required.

Attachments: aurorafield-connector-design.pdf; auth-flow.png

Also: we included a small sample dataset (1000 records) for functional tests; if you need a larger synthetic set we can produce it.

Would prefer Tue 11:00 PDT for the sync.

—Maya

Thanks for the docs, Maya — useful detail.

Proposed validation steps (high level):
1) Pre-flight review (design doc & auth flow) — completed.
2) Sandbox smoke run (functionality + auth checks) — Redwood dev slot.
3) Performance tests (synthetic traces at 1x/3x expected QPS) — capture latency percentiles and KV cache hit behavior.
4) Failure-mode tests (network partitions, token expiry, retrier behavior).
5) Canary on Dedicated pool (limited traffic) with rollback hooks.

Can you provide:
- The sample dataset as a CSV and an expected ranking output for 10 queries?
- A dev API key and a lightweight test harness (curl scripts or Postman collection).

Attached: a suggested test matrix CSV (aurora-test-matrix.csv) with the metrics we collect. We'll use this as the canonical checklist during the sandbox window.

Kimberly Park
Partner Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in a short runbook and compatibility notes from partner engineering: https://redwoodops.company.com/playbooks/partner-onboarding/aurorafield

Key compatibility flags to validate during the sandbox:
- Token-preserving auth: ensure our KV/cache keys are not invalidated by assertion rotation; we will record traces showing cache usage before/after handshake.
- Streaming hooks: confirm that partial response buffering won't block Redwood's batching window (we'll use a 40ms batch gate in sandbox).
- Fallback variants: if adapter fails, verify that Redwood routes to an internal model variant per policy.

Smoke tests (we'll run):
- 50 warmup requests, 200 measured requests at 1rps for functional correctness.
- Inject 5s delay on auth path and confirm graceful degradation policy triggers.

If the smoke passes we'll plan a two-day canary on Dedicated with gradual ramp to 2% of traffic, then 10%.

Sergio Alvarez
Principal Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference
